newsitem.title: UK: Believing makes Mondays blue, study finds.
newsitem.headline: Believing makes Mondays blue, study finds.

text.p: People who believe there is such a thing as "Monday blues" are more likely to be grumpy about Mondays, according to new research by a British psychiatrist.
The study showed that how people expect to feel directly affects how they do feel, Giles Croft of the University of Leeds found.
He told the annual meeting of Britain's Royal Society of Psychiatrists he was able to manipulate how people felt about Mondays.

Croft divided 66 volunteers into three groups. One were given a report saying Monday blues existed, the second a report saying there was no such thing, while the third group got no extra reading material.
Everyone completed a daily mood diary for two weeks, and at the end, rated each day of the week for mood.

The group who got the sceptical report reported more positive emotions and said they felt enthusiastic and inspired more often on Mondays than the "pro-blues" group. There were no differences in negative emotions on Mondays.
But the group that had been told Monday blues were real rated Monday as the worst day of the week.
"They persuaded themselves in hindsight," Croft told the conference.
